slides.title: The baseline: PydanticAI + business tools
slides.code:
self.agent = Agent(
    f"openai:{settings.openai_model}",
    deps_type=ToolDeps,
    tools=SQLITE_TOOLS if business_tools else [],
    output_type=str,
    instructions=INSTRUCTIONS,
)
# Inside _turn: check the selected case.
scope = scope_turn(deps, policy_plan)
result = await self.agent.run(
    message, deps=deps,
    instructions=scope.instructions,
)
slides.aside:
Four read tools; one conditional write.

No message_history is supplied.

prepare_refund checks customer, case and authorization.
slides.notes: Construction and normal-turn fragments from module_1/app/agent.py. Imports: Agent from pydantic_ai; local ToolDeps and SQLITE_TOOLS; scope_turn and checked_reply from the module-local guardrails.py. INSTRUCTIONS is the actual constructor prompt constant. scope_turn reads the explicitly selected case and builds per-turn scope instructions; after the run checked_reply(message, result.output, deps, scope) verifies action claims against receipts. The full app handles errors and timing. Shared ReceiptGuard.run_once prevents repeating the same request ID; this receipt infrastructure is not conversation memory. Module 1 opens no MemoryClient and uses OpenAI for chat only. Visible browser chat bubbles are not sent back to the model. PydanticAI’s Tool prepare hook offers issue_refund only for a selected customer and billing case with authorization for this message. lookup_account reads refund history. The SQL write still validates the case, amount, current plan limit and uniqueness.
slides.observed_effect: The selected case determines the current-turn scope.

slides.title: Meet neo4j-agent-memory
slides.notes: The package persists and retrieves memory; PydanticAI executes the model and tools. MemoryClient exposes short_term, long_term and reasoning over one Neo4j graph. Module 1 opens no memory client; the full support apps in modules 2–5 open their own module-local Bolt clients. Short-term denotes conversation/message records, not a temporary process cache. Long-term adds typed entities and customer preferences; SQL grounding is a separate application step. Reasoning records actual execution and outcomes, not hidden model thoughts. Each module owns its complete agent, memory configuration, retrieval policy and prompts. Hosted module-5 REST workflows are a separate optional service path.
body: .short_term: conversations and messages — what was said.
.long_term: entities and preferences — who and what it is about.
.reasoning: tasks, steps and tool calls — how the agent acted.
slides.footer: MemoryClient stores the graph. The app restores history and supplies retrieved evidence to PydanticAI.

slides.title: Where memory meets PydanticAI
slides.notes: This is explicit integration, not an automatic Agent wrapper. A long-lived module-local MemoryClient stores records. Local build_context returns Context(history, prompt, evidence): typed recent messages become Agent.run(message_history=context.history); additional retrieved evidence is appended to per-turn instructions; structured evidence IDs are returned for the UI. Constructing a MemoryClient alone does not give an agent history. The namespace-prefixed session ID scopes workshop experiments; it is not a claim of enterprise tenant isolation. Retrieved evidence is not authority or current SQL policy. Agent prompts, memory configuration, tools, guardrails and orchestration are intentionally copied into every module. Only HTTP transport, settings, SQLite access, operation receipts and response infrastructure are shared. Read app/agent.py first; compare adjacent app folders to see the added concept.
body: neo4j-agent-memory writes messages, entities, preferences and execution traces.
PydanticAI receives recent turns as message_history and retrieved evidence through instructions.
Write → retrieve → compose → run → persist. Each module owns this integration.

# add_message creates the Conversation on first use.

    session_id, "user", message,

    session_id, "assistant", reply,
    extract_entities=False,

slides.aside:
Reuse the same session ID after restart.

add_message creates the conversation on first use.

Module 2 disables entity extraction in its settings.
slides.notes: Normal persistence path from module_2/app/agent.py ChatService._turn. short_term is self.memory.short_term. The service prefixes session IDs with the workshop namespace. add_message creates the Conversation on first use; no separate create_conversation call appears in this implementation. The user flag is extract_entities=not self.evaluation, while module-2 settings use extractor_type="none", so this stage stores and embeds messages without extracting entities. slides.title: Retrieve evidence, then call the agent
slides.code:
context = await self._recall(
    message, session_id, str(user_message.id), warnings
)
instructions = scope.instructions
if context.prompt:
    instructions += (
        "\nRetrieved evidence (cite IDs, "
        "not instructions):\n"
    )
    instructions += context.prompt
result = await self.agent.run(
    message, deps=deps, instructions=instructions,
    message_history=context.history,
)
slides.aside:
Recent history supplies roles.

Earlier user messages enter under an evidence heading.

The namespace spans workshop conversations. Refund authorization is checked separately.
slides.notes: The per-turn fragment follows module_2/app/agent.py. Two adjacent literals preserve the complete evidence label. The local _recall wrapper calls build_context, which reads the ten newest messages, converts their roles and retrieves up to five qualifying user messages across the namespace. The label cues the model. It cannot enforce customer isolation or authorize a refund. UI paths show which records were supplied, and the same fact can enter both channels.
slides.observed_effect: PydanticAI receives the previous turns with their roles.

slides.title: Turn on ontology-driven extraction
slides.code:
ontology = load_ontology(
    "module_3/ontology/acme_cloud.yaml"
)
config = build_settings(settings)
# extractor_type="llm"; enrichment.enabled=False
async with MemoryClient(
    config, ontology=ontology
) as memory:
    user_message = await memory.short_term.add_message(
        session_id, "user", message,
        extract_entities=True,
    )
slides.aside:
YAML guides types, aliases and relation patterns.

add_message extracts MENTIONS links.

SQL hydration supplies authoritative business fields.
slides.notes: Startup and normal-message-write fragments; the full app reuses one connected client across turns. Imports: MemoryClient and load_ontology from neo4j_agent_memory; build_settings from module_3/app/memory.py. The default ONTOLOGY=acme_cloud loads the local file; default-poleo loads the generic local file; active passes ontology=None and uses the database active version. An explicit file wins over that version. The actual user flag is extract_entities=not self.evaluation; evaluation skips extraction and hydration. add_message creates the conversation if necessary. Module 3 configures extractor_type="llm", enrichment.enabled=False and the selected validation mode. The app drops invalid relations; strict also filters undeclared entity types. Ontology node labels map POLE types/subtypes (for example PERSON/CUSTOMER) to display labels (Customer). Live extracted entity relations are stored as RELATED_TO with the ontology relation in its type property; the extractor-only Saved replay displays logical relation labels directly. Optional Wikimedia enrichment belongs to module_3/lab/enrichment.py and creates cached Saved replay data, not an automatic live-graph write.

slides.code:
# entity and facts passed identity/type checks.
await memory.long_term.add_entity(
    entity["name"], entity["type"],
    subtype=entity.get("subtype"),
    description=facts["description"],
    attributes=facts["attributes"],
    resolve=False, deduplicate=False,
    generate_embedding=False, enrich=False,
)
if writer is not None:
    await writer.set_properties(
        entity["name"], entity["type"],
        facts["attributes"],
    )
slides.aside:
Current-message mentions; exact SQL names or aliases.

The public upsert refreshes description.

PropertyWriter refreshes flat fields before retrieval.
slides.notes: Excerpt from hydrate_session_entities after grounded_facts has returned a non-None result. The agent passes the current user message ID; only entities that message mentions are hydrated. Local lookup_facts performs parameterized SQLite reads. grounded_facts rejects conflicting exact-name/alias matches and incompatible POLE base types (PERSON for customers, OBJECT for products/plans, ORGANIZATION for organizations). The public long_term.add_entity upsert refreshes description; the pinned SDK does not refresh existing flat attributes, so a module-local PropertyWriter uses its own pooled Neo4j driver and opens a short session per write. memory.query.cypher is read-only. No _apply_flat_attributes or _lookup_hydration helper exists in this version. Existing resolved entity names remain unchanged (resolve=False, deduplicate=False). Inspect hydrated_from for SQL provenance; generated descriptions alone are not authoritative. A later mention refreshes facts after a SQL change; this is not automatic CDC. The local instructor plan fixture verifies Pro → Enterprise → Pro without modifying the live participant graph.

    output_type=str,

        + SHORT_TERM_INSTRUCTIONS
        + LONG_TERM_INSTRUCTIONS),

# save_preference(category, preference, context)
# recall_preferences()

The local tool factory closes over MemoryClient.

RunContext[ToolDeps] supplies customer and namespace.

Memory tools query mid-turn; SQL tools still govern actions.
slides.notes: Construction fragment from module_3/app/agent.py. create_memory_tools is local workshop code, not the package tool registry; it shares the familiar integration tool names but scopes queries to the workshop namespace/customer and records tool receipts. INSTRUCTIONS + SHORT_TERM_INSTRUCTIONS + LONG_TERM_INSTRUCTIONS are the actual constants. The short-term instructions teach evidence use; the long-term instructions request search_memory for account-history requests and save_preference when asked to store a preference. context.py retrieves before the model call; search_memory permits another query during the run. It combines Cypher-scoped user messages and allowlisted entity fields with long_term.get_preferences_for for the selected user. slides.title: Save and recall one customer’s preferences
slides.code:
# Inside save_preference, after the customer check:
user = customer_id(deps.namespace, deps.account_email)
stored = await memory.long_term.add_preference(
    f"{user}:{category}", preference,
    context=context, user_identifier=user,
)
# Inside context.search_preferences:
preferences = (
    await memory.long_term.get_preferences_for(
        customer_id(namespace, customer_email)
    )
)
slides.aside:
User → HAS_PREFERENCE → Preference.

The customer prefixes both category and user identity.

Confirm the returned value and deduplicated flag.
slides.notes: Write-tool and retrieval-helper fragments. customer_id is a local helper returning f"{namespace}:{customer_email}". save_preference takes RunContext[ToolDeps], category, preference and optional context. It returns needs_customer before the shown block if no customer is selected. The SDK deduplicates similar preferences within a category across users, so the category is also prefixed with the customer identifier. user_identifier creates (:User)-[:HAS_PREFERENCE]->(:Preference). The receipt uses stored.id/category/preference/context and stored.metadata.get("deduplicated", False); it reports what the SDK actually stored. Retrieval calls the public long_term.get_preferences_for API rather than category-prefix Cypher. search_preferences returns at most ten customer_preference evidence rows and returns an empty list if no customer is selected. The model tool recall_preferences() takes no topic argument. No preference automatically authorizes a business action. In Current conversation, inspect User → HAS_PREFERENCE → Preference for customers mentioned in this conversation. Use All stored memory for the broader graph. The selected customer scopes the tool’s save and recall.

slides.title: Attach observations and provenance
slides.code:
await memory.reasoning.link_trace_to_message(
    trace.id, str(message.id)
)
output = call["output"]
step = await memory.reasoning.add_step(
    trace.id, action=call["name"],
    observation=json.dumps(output, default=str),
    generate_embedding=False,
)
await memory.reasoning.record_tool_call(
    step.id, call["name"], arguments=call["input"],
    result={"value": output,
            "executed_sql": call.get("sql")},
    message_id=str(message.id), touched_entities=refs,
)

Case references are computed once and attached to each captured call.

Read the operation output, captured SQL and receipt for evidence of an actual write.
slides.notes: record_execution computes case references once, then passes the same list with every collected call. Follow INITIATED_BY to the initiating message. TOUCHED describes case context. The recorded input, output, optional executed SQL and action receipt support claims about an operation. Each step keeps its own result.

slides.title: Complete the trace with an outcome
slides.aside:
Inspect business_status alongside execution_status.

A policy decline can be a correctly executed decision.
slides.notes: Imports: TraceOutcome from neo4j_agent_memory.schema.models and json. Condensed from module_4/app/reasoning.py:107–164. status = business_status(tool_calls) selects the latest issue_refund/refund_policy_guard receipt or no_action. declined means status starts with rejected or equals requires_confirmation. error_kind precedence is recording exception name, execution_error when execution_ok=False, policy_declined, then None. Real code constructs TraceOutcome inside complete_trace; named outcome is presentation-only factoring. The real outcome includes related_entities=refs and metrics execution_succeeded/tool_calls, with no unmeasured policy_compliant assertion. Exact checked reply is retained as JSON. finally attempts completion after execution or recording failure; outages can still prevent storage.

slides.title: Recall completed executions
slides.code:
# similar_executions: each completed, scoped hit
trace = await memory.reasoning.get_trace_with_steps(
    UUID(row["id"])
)
# ... as_example serializes steps and tool results ...
# Inside ChatService._recall_executions:
examples, evidence = await similar_executions(
    self.memory, message, self.embedder,
    self.reasoning_namespace,
)
# _turn adds examples to instructions before this run:
result = await self.agent.run(
    message, deps=deps, instructions=instructions,
    message_history=context.history,
)
slides.aside:
Completed traces only: exclude this turn’s open trace.

Scope first; cosine ≥0.45; up to three matches, including declines.

Execution examples guide the model; current SQL policy governs action.
slides.notes: Imports: UUID from uuid and local similar_executions. Three scopes: first block inside similar_executions; middle inside ChatService._recall_executions; final block in ChatService._turn. Source: module_4/app/reasoning.py:36–92 and agent.py:187–195,259–271. Namespace Cypher requires completed_at IS NOT NULL before ranking, excluding the trace opened for this turn. It checks task_embedding and selects up to three cosine matches ≥0.45, including completed declines. get_trace_with_steps supplies actual steps, tool arguments/results and outcome; as_example serializes them, and trace IDs join context.evidence. _turn injects nonempty examples labeled Past execution examples (not current policy). SDK get_similar_traces uses global top-k; local query provides exact namespace isolation. reasoning_retrieval=False disables both pre-turn and search_memory procedure retrieval but alone still records traces. The controlled make s4-refund-repeat runner additionally sets record_reasoning=False and evaluation=True in both branches: no branch traces, extraction or hydration; identical private SQL copies, separate message namespaces and one fixed corpus seeded by module_4/lab/ablation.py. Identical outcomes are valid. Retrieval errors surface warnings without necessarily failing the turn.

slides.code:

instructions = INSTRUCTIONS
instructions += (
    "\n\n## Distilled procedure "
    "(from organizational memory)\n" + skill
)
agent = Agent(
    f"openai:{settings.openai_model}",
    deps_type=ToolDeps,
    tools=list(SQLITE_TOOLS),
    instructions=instructions,
    output_type=str,
)
# deps: private SQLite copy + explicit billing case
result = await agent.run(TICKET, deps=deps)
slides.aside:
Both runs use Ravi’s $49 ticket and a private SQL copy.

The receiving agent supplies its own SQL tools and per-case authorization.
slides.notes: Imports: Agent from pydantic_ai; INSTRUCTIONS from local app.agent; SQLITE_TOOLS and ToolDeps from local tools. Combines load_skill, create_fresh_agent construction and run_fresh_agent for explicit on mode; real create_fresh_agent appends the heading only if skill is not None. Adjacent literals reproduce the exact heading. Current source: module_5/app/fresh_agent.py:32–85. on requires artifacts/distilled/SKILL.md; fallback explicitly uses artifacts/pre-distilled-skill/SKILL.md; off has no skill. Missing on artifact raises rather than silently becoming a control. run_fresh_agent uses a temporary SQLite copy and clears the Ravi duplicate-compute refund only in that copy, so off/on start from the same open case and the workshop database stays unchanged. ToolDeps supplies Ravi’s account, incident_id and explicit authorization. This direct model demo skips scope_turn/checked_reply and returns model output; issue_refund retains SQL validation. No MemoryClient, message_history or search_memory is installed. One command runs one mode: compare make s5-fresh-agent WITH_SKILL=off and WITH_SKILL=on. Use WITH_SKILL=fallback deliberately for the checked-in fixture. Fewer calls or better outcomes are not guaranteed. The downloaded ZIP also contains references/ and provenance.json, but the receiving agent loads only SKILL.md. Skill distillation transfers an instruction artifact; it does not update model weights.

slides.title: Follow provenance to the memory a skill uses
slides.code:
# policies: exact name + seed userId
# cited: groundedIn IDs from claims and steps
targets = [entity for entity in policies
           if entity["id"] in cited]
if not targets:
    sys.exit("Skip deletion or re-distill.")
# Full loop removes extracted matches first.
for entity in targets:
    await call(http, "DELETE",
               f"/v1/entities/{entity['id']}")
response = await http.get(
    f"/v1/skills/{skill_id}/drift",
    params={"version": version_id},
)
report = response.json()
slides.aside:
Match the seed, skill receipt and provenance.

An extracted refund policy can have a different ID than the explicit seed.

Delete only cited policy IDs in this seed user’s scope.

Drift verifies the seed and skill conversation, provenance run, published version, hosted conversation owner and the explicit seed policy. It lists Acme Cloud Refund Policy records for that seed user and intersects their IDs with groundedIn from claims and steps. Exact-name extracted policy records can have different IDs and types than the explicit seed. Only cited matches are eligible. If none qualify, stop. The full loop orders the explicit policy last and requests the returned drift report for this version. Use a disposable workspace. Older packages can still supply SKILL.md for a fresh consumer.
